text: dsh-plugin-chatgpt 是 DeepSeek Harness 的 ChatGPT 模型提供方，适用于 Web 客户端：它注册 chatgpt 模型路由，并在“设置 → 模型”提供账户卡片。用户可通过 ChatGPT OAuth 登录，浏览账户可用的模型，在模型选择器中调用订阅支持的模型；插件还转换 DSH 请求和流式响应，并显示账户计划与模型数量。适合希望在 DSH 中使用现有 ChatGPT 订阅的人。使用前需要可用的 ChatGPT 账户，不需要单独配置 API Key。

dsh-plugin-chatgpt adds a ChatGPT provider route and account card to DeepSeek Harness. Sign in through OAuth, view the models available to the account, and use the subscription-backed provider for DSH requests. It requires a ChatGPT account, not a separate API key.

Can I use my ChatGPT plan as a model provider in DSH?
I want DSH to list the models available to my signed-in ChatGPT account.
ChatGPT 登录：从模型设置卡片启动 OAuth，使用本机回调完成授权，也可粘贴重定向地址或授权码；凭据由主机端保存。
账户模型列表：登录后读取订阅账户可用模型，并将其加入 DSH 模型选择器；模型名称、上下文窗口和推理级别来自账户列表或目录。
订阅模型推理：DSH 请求被转换为 Responses API 输入，插件发送请求并逐段转发流式响应，遇到缺少终止事件会报告失败。
上下文预算配置：可为所有模型设置统一预算，或按准确模型 ID 设置覆盖值；路由注册时将这些设置应用到模型元数据。
账户状态与登出：设置卡片展示账户状态、计划及可用模型数量；用户可结束账户会话并查看服务器是否确认撤销。
dsh-plugin-chatgpt 使用前须知：模型请求会携带访问令牌发送到 OpenAI 的 api.openai.com；OAuth 授权和令牌交换连接 auth.openai.com。
dsh-plugin-chatgpt 使用前须知：登录凭据持久化在配置的 stateDir 下，默认目录由 DSH_HOME 或 HOME 推导；需要本机目录可写。

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · dsh-plugin-chatgpt：Adds one DeepSeek Harness provider route, `chatgpt`, that answers model calls from a signed-in ChatGPT subscription rather than an API key. Signing in uses OpenAI's published *Sign in with ChatGPT* flow, so the account's own plan pays for inference. The route is named `chatgpt` and not `openai` because the built-in pi-ai plugin already owns that name. Models, their context windows, and their reasoning levels come from your account's own listing, so the roster follows your plan rather than a hard-coded list.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Install into a profile：The whole install is one line:

```text
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-plugin-chatgpt
```

Restart the harness afterwards: a profile is composed at startup. Removing it:

```text
dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-plugin-chatgpt
```

The package is on npm, so the registry is the whole install and no build step is involved:

```text
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-plugin-chatgpt@0.1.9   # pin a version, or omit it for the latest
```

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Install into a profile：Installing from a repository URL instead builds from source, and pnpm refuses a git dependency's build scripts until they are allowlisted: `add https://github.com/ckanner/dsh-plugin-chatgpt` fails with `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED` until `dsh-plugin-chatgpt` is approved under `onlyBuiltDependencies` in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Install into a profile：The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so adding it appends the bundle to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` and inserts its row into the composition. Verify the layer without booting:

```text
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config   # shows a "# == dsh-plugin-chatgpt" layer
```

A package installing without a `dsh.bundle` declaration activates no layer; `dsh plugin` warns instead.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Sign in：Open **Settings → Models**. The plugin owns a **ChatGPT** row, and the card on that row offers **Sign in with ChatGPT**. The card shows the authorization URL and selects it for copying, accepts the final redirect URL pasted back when the browser cannot reach the loopback address, and afterwards reports the account — its plan, the token's next refresh, and how many models it offers — with a **Sign out** button. No token reaches the page.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Sign in：Signing out revokes the renewable session at the authorization server before clearing it locally, and says so when the server did not confirm.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Sign in：The grant is stored owner-only under `stateDir`. `attempt.submit()` rejects a malformed or mismatched value and leaves the attempt open, so a mistyped paste can be corrected. -----

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · What you get：One provider route, listed in **Settings → Models** like any built-in provider, with the model roster, context windows, and reasoning levels the account is entitled to. Selecting a model there is what puts it in the model selector; no separate picker is involved.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · What you get：Model metadata comes from the account listing. By default the adapter follows each model's advertised context window, including updates when the catalog refreshes. Set `contextWindowLimit` for a global budget or `modelContextWindowLimits` for individual models; explicit values are used as-is. Sign-in lives on that row's card.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · What you get：For example, add this field to the plugin's configuration to set DSH's context budget to 1,000,000 tokens for models without an individual override, even if the catalog reports a maximum of 872,000. Remove it to restore account defaults for those models. These settings are independent of Codex settings. DSH still reserves headroom for compaction; they do not change service-side request limits.

```yaml
contextWindowLimit: 1000000
```

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · What you get：For separate model budgets, use exact model IDs as dictionary keys. The priority is individual model, then global budget, then account default. In this example Astra uses 1,000,000, Sol uses 800,000, and other models use 500,000. The global field is optional; omit it to let other models follow their account defaults.

```yaml
contextWindowLimit: 500000
modelContextWindowLimits:
  gpt-6-astra: 1000000
  gpt-6.1-sol: 800000

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · What you get：Changes take effect the next time DSH resolves a model. Removing a model entry restores the current global budget, or its account default when no global budget is set. Keys are case-sensitive exact IDs, not display names or wildcard patterns. The share of the plan this installation may spend is set per app, in ChatGPT settings: -----

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Understand the implementation：- A request never carries `temperature`, `max_output_tokens`, `top_p`, `truncation`, or the other fields the plan-usage route refuses. They are named in `REFUSED_FIELDS` so they cannot be reintroduced by accident.
- `response.completed` is the only successful terminal. A stream that ends without one is an error, because a truncated answer that reads as finished is worse than a visible failure.
- **Account metadata is read at run time.** The plugin requests `GET /v1/models` with the selected account's grant. The bundled catalog fills missing metadata, and the dated measured list can add unlisted models. Model availability and context capacity are separate from the context budget reported to DSH.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Model Experience：This bundle inserts one provider row, and that row's plugin owns all of its model-facing behaviour; the layer itself contributes no prompt, tool, or context of its own.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · What the model sees：For every turn routed to `chatgpt`, the adapter preserves the order of messages, assistant blocks, tool calls, and results. System and developer instructions become developer messages at their original positions. DSH is told to append system-prompt updates in history. Native assistant output, including encrypted reasoning, is retained in DSH's `replayState` and replayed for the same authorization, route, and model when the saved content is unchanged.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Token effect：Variable. Visible context comes from DSH. Replaying encrypted reasoning can also contribute input tokens; a readable reasoning summary is not a substitute. The adapter does not truncate history: DSH owns compaction using the reported context budget. Output reservations are kept below that budget, but this route does not accept an output-token cap.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · KV Cache effect：The adapter preserves reusable prefixes and opaque reasoning across tool turns and session restore. A bounded hash of the local authorization namespace, client registration, endpoint, provider, session ID, and call purpose supplies both `prompt_cache_key` and the `session_id` header; token refresh does not change it. Reauthorization gets a fresh namespace; legacy grants acquire one on first load. Sessionless calls omit these identifiers. OpenAI handles cache routing automatically on GPT-5.6 and later; a key is not a cache-hit guarantee. The SIWC route requires `store: false` and full HTTP history; response storage and prompt caching are separate. Cache retention/options remain omitted, as in Pi's public SIWC path, pending model-and-route-specific validation. See the [official caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) and [reasoning replay guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning#preserve-reasoning-without-stored-responses).

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Existing histories remain usable** — older sessions have no encrypted replay state to recover. Their visible messages and tools are replayed in order. Edited, pruned, foreign, malformed, or incompatible replay metadata falls back to visible history without reintroducing discarded content. This integration requires a DSH host supporting `finish.replayState` and `systemPromptUpdate: "in-history"`; see [the replay design and validation plan](docs/cache-replay.md).

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **One account at a time in the UI** — the host keeps every authorized account separate and can sign one out by subject, but the card shows and switches only the active account, so adding a second one means signing out first.
- **Images and files are not sent** — an image or file block carries a durable attachment reference that this adapter does not resolve, so it reaches the model as the placeholder text `[image omitted: not yet supported]`. The omission is visible rather than silent, but the content is genuinely lost.
- **The plan-usage route is in preview** — computer use, Code Interpreter, file search, hosted MCP, image generation, and `tool_search` are refused upstream regardless of what this plugin sends, and `multi_agent`, `temperature`, and `max_output_tokens` are among fifteen fields that must be omitted.
- **The roster mixes two sources with different authority** — the account's listing supplies advertised models with the endpoint's own metadata; the models this route measurably serves but the listing omits are added from `src/models/served.ts`, dated by when they were measured. dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Context growth has a configurable budget** — the default follows each model's account-catalog window, without a shared fixed cap. `contextWindowLimit` and every `modelContextWindowLimits` value must be safe integers of at least 1,024 tokens. Individual model values override the global value; both take precedence over catalog metadata without clamping, following Pi's override behavior. Without an override, missing account metadata uses the bundled fallback. DSH's own compaction policy controls the actual trigger and headroom. This is a context budget, not a hard spending limit or a cache-hit target.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Signing out is two things, and the card says which happened** — the renewable session is revoked at the authorization server before the credential is cleared here, because a grant deleted locally may still be live elsewhere. When the server cannot be reached the sign-out still completes locally, and the outcome says the remote revocation was not confirmed. An exhausted allowance names ChatGPT's own usage page and says that the code identifies neither the cause nor a reset time: the plan's shared usage and an app-specific limit are both possible, which is why a plan that looks well within its limits on the site and a refusal can both be true.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Every Config field is `volatile()`, and that is load-bearing** — the harness builds a plugin's settings form from its volatile fields alone, and a plugin with none gets no settings namespace. The Models page renders a provider row only for a row whose namespace exists, so a schema without a volatile field leaves the route, and the card that rides it, impossible to display. Volatile fields are read through `.get()` at the point of use rather than captured as values.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **The Client half mounts its own Remote namespace** — a bundled third-party plugin cannot reach `ctx.remote.<namespace>` on its own: the Gateway installs a namespace only from a contribution of generated descriptors, and the package carrying those for the shipped API packages is generated at build time from a fixed list of workspace packages. Nothing generates one for an out-of-tree package, and the generator is not published, so this plugin mounts the contribution itself from `src/remote-methods.ts`. A test reads the controller's source and fails when the two lists drift, because a method added on one side only would fail at the moment a user clicks.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Signing in announces the new roster to the browser** — a model selector caches the Host catalog and reloads it only when the Host says something changed, so a plugin that fills an empty roster at sign-in time has to publish `llm/adapters-updated`. Without it the models are served and never appear in the selector, which looks exactly like a broken provider. The account card reports how many models the account offers, or why the listing could not be read.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Cache statistics are measured, not predicted** — the percentage is `cacheReadTokens / (inputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheWriteTokens)` using provider-reported counters. Earlier versions reordered tool history and dropped native reasoning; their low hit rates do not establish an inherent SIWC limit. Prefix-preservation tests do not measure live cache hits. Compare fixed-model, fixed-effort runs after warm-up, recording cache reads/writes, total input, latency, and quota impact.

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Each installation registers its own client** — ChatGPT settings lists one app row per registration, named by `agent_name_hint`, and this plugin keeps the account/client mapping after signing out so the next sign-in on the same installation reuses its row instead of adding another. A second state directory is a second installation to OpenAI, and registers separately; deleting a state directory is what forgets one.

npm run build     # tsc emits the host half and the declarations, esbuild the browser bundle

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Dev Note：`dev-types/` holds development-only declarations for the harness's LLM and Cordis seams, transcribed from the harness sources. They are not published and never shipped; the host supplies the real packages as peer dependencies. An end-to-end mount in a real harness remains the authoritative check.

Regenerate the model catalog when the upstream catalog moves:

```text
node scripts/generate-model-catalog.mjs /path/to/@earendil-works/pi-ai
```

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Releasing：A release is one tag: bump the version, push the tag, and the release workflow runs every check the CI lane runs, publishes only when the registry does not have that version yet, and records the GitHub Release either way.

```text
npm version 0.1.14
git push --follow-tags
```

dsh-plugin-chatgpt README · Releasing：Publishing takes either the repository's `NPM_TOKEN` secret or npm trusted publishing (workflow `release.yml`); the Release half uses the run's own token. Asking the registry first is what lets a tag for a version that was published by hand record its Release instead of failing, and what lets re-running a tag repair a missing Release. `workflow_dispatch` releases the manifest's version, creating the tag when it is absent.
